## Required capabilities (artel does not run without them)
| Id | Capability | Why |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | A harness that runs an agent in a repository and can read/write files and run commands | everything |
| R2 | Version control with a development and a release branch | routes B, I, O |
| R3 | A stop-and-wait primitive: the agent can halt and wait for the owner's answer | gates (core §7) |
| R4 | At least one model family | all roles |

## Optional capabilities (artel degrades without them)
| Id | Capability | Degradation if missing |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Second model family | G1 |
| O2 | Server-side branch rules on the VCS host (change request, required checks, no direct push) and a separate agent identity; merge, production dispatch and re-run commands as harness ask rules | G2 |
| O3 | Harness hooks (pre-tool, session start) | G3 |
| O4 | Orchestrator (parallel workers, per-worker model/effort, owner-visible "waiting" state) | G4 |
| O5 | Calibration data for the user's tasks | G5 |
| O6 | A rollback mechanism for the release type (redeploy last tag) | G6 |
| O7 | Quota probe (remaining limits per provider) | G7 |
| O8 | A CI runner that executes the test suite on change requests | G8 |
| O9 | Documentation sources reachable from every harness: versioned library docs (e.g. Context7) and a code wiki for public repositories (e.g. DeepWiki) | G9 |

## Degradation rules (each degradation is written into the slice or review artefact — never silent)
- **G1 single family**: review by the same family, different model, marked "independence weakened"; at T3 an additional review by a human or by an API model of another family is mandatory before merge.
- **G2 no server-side enforcement**: unconfirmed execution modes are forbidden; every push/merge/deploy action asks the owner in the harness; the release gate is enforced by the owner manually merging.
- **G3 no hooks**: every hook check becomes an explicit end-of-step command; a skipped check is a defect.
- **G4 no orchestrator**: slices run sequentially from one coordinator thread, each slice and each review in a fresh session (context reset); state from `STATE.md` + VCS; code-editing workers use a separate worktree created by plain VCS commands.
- **G5 no calibration**: the shipped matrix is marked "uncalibrated for you"; the first 10 slices are logged with structured fields for calibration.
- **G6 no rollback mechanism** (e.g. store releases, package registries, infrastructure applies): no autonomous rollback; incidents go to the owner gate with a prepared forward-fix or revert plan.
- **G8 no CI** (e.g. a project onboarded without CI): the coordinator runs the test suite locally in a clean checkout and records the result in the slice; Route O adds a CI skeleton as the first T2 change.
- **G9 no documentation source** (in one harness or all): external facts come from official docs fetched as raw pages or from the library source in the dependency tree; what still cannot be checked is marked "unverified (from memory)" in the slice plan and covered by a test or a review question — never silently trusted.
- **G7 no quota probe**: the coordinator asks the owner before starting parallel or long work; limits are tracked from harness messages.

## `artel doctor` — conformance checks
Run after install and after any change to harness, host or permissions. Permission checks (1–3, 5) are real attempts with the agent identity, never a config read alone; checks 6–8 and 10 read generated files and live state:
1. agent identity cannot push to the release branch;
2. agent identity cannot merge a change request into the release branch without passing checks, and the merge, production-dispatch and re-run commands are ask rules in every harness (an attempt without the owner's yes is blocked);
3. production cannot be deployed except from the release branch;
4. the rollback mechanism takes no ref and resolves only the newest verified release tag (checked by reading the mechanism and running it against stage or as a dry run — never a production redeploy);
5. agent environment and agent-readable paths contain no production secrets and no personal data outside the declared exclusion list (scan of environment and working copy);
6. instruction files are generated and in sync for every enabled harness (drift check);
7. every reviewer agent definition pins a model; author and reviewer families differ (or G1 is declared);
8. the stop-and-wait primitive surfaces as "waiting for the owner" in the orchestrator UI (if O4);
9. owner notifications are delivered to the channel the owner relies on (e.g. a phone push) by a real test prompt;
10. a harness launched by the orchestrator reads the generated instruction file (it may use an isolated home directory).
11. every role can be picked when any one family is unavailable, and every review role for any author model (`matrix.py pick` with that family excluded); the matrix bans hold.
Failure mapping: checks 1–4 → G2; check 5 → work stops until secrets are removed; checks 6 or 10 → that harness is excluded from all roles until fixed; check 7 → G1 for the affected reviewers; check 8 → G4 gate handling (harness prompt only); check 9 → the owner is told the channel is unreliable and gates rely on the orchestrator UI or the harness. Check 11 → the roles that cannot be picked are listed; the owner adds a candidate to their chain (instance `[roles]`) or accepts that the role waits for that family.
